title: Fundamental Values of Democracy
shortDescription: Liberty, equality, justice, fraternity, rule of law and how Indian democracy embodies them.
genZNote: Democracy is more than voting day. It's a bundle of values — and the Preamble hands them to you in four words.

sections.heading: Core Values
bullets: Liberty (freedom of thought, expression, belief, faith, worship); Equality (of status and opportunity); Justice (social, economic, political); Fraternity (dignity of individual and unity and integrity of the nation) — all in the Preamble.
Rule of law, pluralism, participation, accountability, transparency and dignity.
Abraham Lincoln's definition: government of the people, by the people, for the people.

sections.heading: Forms of Democracy and Features
bullets: Features: free and fair periodic elections, universal adult franchise (Art. 326), independent judiciary, free press, protection of minorities, constitutional limits on power.
Political equality: "one person, one vote, one value".

sections.heading: Ambedkar on Social Democracy
sections.body: In his closing speech (25 November 1949) Dr. B. R. Ambedkar warned that political democracy cannot last unless it rests on social democracy — liberty, equality and fraternity as an inseparable trinity — and that India faced a contradiction between political equality and social and economic inequality.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Democratic values — liberty, equality, justice and fraternity — guide Indian governance and are embedded in the Preamble.

commonTraps: Do not confuse republic with democracy — both are in the Preamble.

sources.name: NCERT, Indian Constitution at Work (Class XI Political Science)
